title: Add parent-branch executor for stacked Work Item closure
outOfScope: Closing a Work Item from an arbitrary repository or unregistered worktree.
Deleting any branch before merged-PR and receipt verification succeeds.
Release publication or unrelated WI-10 installation documentation changes.

sources.reason: The current CLI requires the caller to run the branch-local script, which prevents a newer parent branch from closing an already-merged child worktree that still has the prior script version.
Existing lifecycle tests establish strict merged-PR, SHA, receipt, deletion, and stacked-parent boundaries.
Archived child Work Item evidence and merged PR #474 provide the real recovery target.
The prior corrective repair records the retained-merge proof but exposes the need for a parent-branch execution entrypoint.

PR #473 proves that the aggregate checker cannot distinguish a verified historical recovery chain from unrelated newly maintained Work Items when an earlier archived Contract lacks an explicit predecessor source.
Existing aggregate PR tests cover source-linked recovery chains but not an append-only receipt that verifies an immutable historical chain without rewriting archives.

riskAssessment.reason: An unvalidated target worktree could cause closure actions in the wrong checkout, while an over-broad aggregate exception could conceal unrelated Work Items. The executor and receipt must be evidence-bound and retain every existing closure and PR-ownership gate.

executionDecision.reason: The user continuously authorized correction of discovered workflow defects before progressing to WI-10 and release work.

preReviewWarnings: Verify that --worktree scopes Git operations but never scopes provider gh requests.
Verify the target is a registered worktree of this repository and that direct default-base closure remains strict.
Verify that a historical recovery receipt cannot waive missing, reordered, incompatible, or unrelated Work Items.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The closure CLI accepts an explicit target worktree only after proving that it is a registered worktree of this repository.
Provider gh requests remain unscoped while every Git operation for the target Work Item runs in the explicit target worktree.
A parent-branch invocation can close archived merged PR #474 from its still-identifiable child worktree and records a valid Closure Receipt.
Default-base closure, arbitrary-path rejection, detached-target rejection, and the existing stacked-parent checks remain fail-closed.
The English and Japanese lifecycle references document the exceptional command without presenting it as a routine adopter path.

The aggregate PR checker accepts a multi-archive PR only when an append-only historical recovery receipt exactly binds the consecutive archived pairs and their Git ancestry; it otherwise retains the one-new-Work-Item rejection.
The receipt and regression tests prove that missing, reordered, incompatible, or unrelated archive entries remain rejected.
guidelines: The explicit target-worktree path must be evidence-bound and fail closed; it is not a general branch deletion API.
Provider operations and Git worktree selection must remain separated so that --worktree cannot alter the provider identity query.
Document the exceptional recovery command in English and Japanese without weakening the normal one-Work-Item lifecycle.
A recovery-chain receipt must bind every historical archive pair and Git relationship deterministically; it must never be a task-name whitelist or require rewriting immutable archive evidence.

intent.problem: After #475 merged, its improved stacked-base validator is available on the WI-10 parent branch, but the older merged child #474 still owns a worktree containing its pre-fix script. The normal closure command therefore cannot execute the new parent-branch implementation against that child checkout. In addition, PR #473 fails because the aggregate checker reads three archived Work Items as independent even though they form a historically merged recovery chain; the first corrective archive cannot be retroactively amended to cite WI-10.
constraints: Keep the default invocation and default-base validation unchanged.
Require the target path to be a registered worktree of the same repository.
Do not scope GitHub provider requests to the target worktree.
Do not delete remote or local branches until the existing authoritative PR and Closure Receipt validations pass.
Do not rewrite any archived Contract, Summary, Start Receipt, or Closure Receipt.
Do not weaken the default one-new-Work-Item-per-PR rule or add a task-name whitelist.
Use the recovered #474 worktree as end-to-end proof after this corrective Work Item merges.
intent.rationale: A narrow, explicit executor lets the synchronized parent branch run current closure policy against a still-identifiable child worktree. A separately append-only, deterministic receipt gives the PR checker a way to verify the historical chain without mutating archive evidence or weakening branch-deletion and PR-ownership controls.

rawUserRequest: Continue: fully solve the stacked PR lifecycle process problem before WI-10 and later release work.

rawRequestSource.reference: conversation:2026-07-30 continuous authorization to correct discovered process defects

declaredIntent.summary: Add a fail-closed parent-branch executor for closing a verified child Work Item worktree.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The parent branch invokes closure for merged child #474 through its registered child worktree.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Closure verifies the exact child PR and parent retention, writes a receipt in the current policy checkout, and deletes only the child branch.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Regression test plus post-merge execution against the preserved #474 worktree.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An arbitrary, detached, or foreign target path is supplied.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Closure stops before provider queries, receipt creation, or branch deletion.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Regression tests for non-worktree and detached target paths.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: PR #473 contains WI-10 and two sequential corrective archive pairs whose earliest correction cannot cite WI-10 because the archive is immutable.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A complete append-only recovery receipt permits only that fully verified historical chain; default multi-Work-Item rejection remains in effect for every other PR.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused aggregate checker tests cover valid chain, missing receipt, reordered entry, incompatible base, and unrelated entry.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Set only when a human explicitly approves restricted governance paths.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
